questions: Did line_loss_events fall to zero or near zero on the s-bend and slalom compared with iteration 0 (1.0 each)?
Did max_error drop below 0.06 m, and did any track get past the 0.06 m off-track limit?
Does the seven-sensor array give a usable signal scale, or does the controller need weights that are not proportional to x?
Is steering_oscillation higher or lower than iteration 0 (0.14 to 0.16)? If higher without line loss, forward offset is the next lever.
Does wheel_track 0.12 m with 0.8 kg still limit turn rate on the slalom?
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors. Also the kp range that gave the best rms_error, and which sensors carry most of the signal when on the line.

intent: Widen the sensor array from ±0.030 m to ±0.042 m footprint edge (seven 12 mm sensors at 12 mm pitch) so the tape stays detected through the 4 cm error zone where iteration 0 lost the line. Hold all other geometry constant to isolate the span effect. Expect fewer line-loss events, max_error under 0.06 m, and first completions on the oval and s-bend.
learning: Iteration 0 showed off-track failure with max_error at the 0.06 m limit and line loss preceding it on all tracks. The body-width limit is floored at 0.06 m for any allowed body width, so sensor span, not body width, is the lever for line retention. Hypothesis 1 (wider span) is now under test. Hypotheses 2 (forward offset 0.05 m) and 3 and 4 (wheel track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg) remain for later iterations, depending on whether this race shows oscillation or slow completion.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced 60 trials with zero completions. All 60 ended off-track, and progress stalled at 0.11 to 0.22. The failure mode is consistent: max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.064 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, and line_loss_events average 1.0 to 1.8 per run. The robot loses the tape at about 4 cm lateral error, then the line-loss recovery cannot bring it back before it passes 6 cm. That points at sensing footprint, not the controller alone. The current five 12 mm sensors at 12 mm pitch span only ±0.030 m of outer footprint edge. A tape edge at 0.0125 m half-width therefore leaves the array once the robot is about 0.04 m off centre. Widening the array is the lever the Integrator's requested change (1) names, and the race data supports it, since line loss precedes off-track on all three tracks. I checked body_width: the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + w/4), which for any w up to 0.18 is 0.06 m, so widening the body gains nothing and I keep 0.12 m. I change one geometry variable: seven 12 mm sensors at 12 mm pitch, x = -0.036 to +0.036, y = 0.03. This extends the outer footprint edge to ±0.042 m, past the point where line loss begins, and keeps the footprints contiguous so the sum of readings stays above 0.05 across the array. I hold forward offset (0.03 m), wheel track (0.12 m), radius (0.03 m) and mass (0.8 kg) fixed, so the next race isolates the span effect. Expected result: line_loss_events drop toward zero on the s-bend and slalom, max_error falls below the 0.06 m limit, and at least the oval and s-bend reach completion or get much further. If oscillation rises with no line loss, the next step is the forward offset (0.05 m) per hypothesis 2.
